objective: Measure how augmenting the E. editha species-wide frozen HOSTS repertoire with exactly two locally documented Castilleja species changes native and contemporary botanical resource geography and reliance on introduced Plantago, without inferring local butterfly demography.

literature_host_additions.scope: locally documented host, not proof of global use

botanical_rules: Find each exact accepted WCVP species binomial and unique accepted ID; ambiguous, synonym-only or missing matches must be disclosed and excluded, not silently resolved. Use frozen extant, non-doubtful level3 WCVP region records, introduced=0 for native and all for contemporary. No genus-level imputation.
analysis_rules: Preserve the 30 exact original host IDs and baseline 131/245/114 footprint unmodified.
Add up to two exact independently documented host IDs in an explicitly labeled augmented butterfly-only sensitivity.
Recompute native and contemporary union and contemporary-minus-native added regions; report counts and identities of gains/losses.

Remove only WCVP introduced-only Plantago lanceolata units in both baseline and augmented reconstructions, retaining its native distribution and other mapped hosts. Measure lost added regions before and after.
Report Castilleja native, contemporary and introduced region counts; if any host has no usable WCVP record, do not assume presence or absence.
Do not reinterpret native WCVP botany as proof of local alternate host availability or developmental suitability.
Do not select additional plants after seeing changes, sweep host sets, or modify the GEB figures/primary results.
outcomes: Plantago unique introduced contribution count and fraction
which previously known added regions were rescued by augmented other host ranges
result_status: If matched, sensitivity of host-database completeness for ONE butterfly, not 239-butterfly global estimate; not a new ecological mechanism or independent confirmatory test.
